frozen_summary_passages.text:
- 5b. Shuffle the **Base Conservation Project cards** and keep them face down next to the board. In a 4-player game place the 4 topmost face up below the board; otherwise the 3 topmost.
   - 5c. **2-player game only:** take 6 player tokens of an unused color and cover: on the face-up Base Conservation Project cards, the left level on the left card, the middle level on the middle card, and the right level on the right card; and on the Association board, the three spaces in the left column of the donation area. Covered levels/spaces are blocked and cannot be used by either player.

- **C2.** Place 7 player tokens on the designated spaces at the left edge of your zoo map; keep the rest next to your map for later use.
  - **C3.** Place 1 association worker on the notepad of your zoo map (the active worker) and the remaining 3 lying down on the designated spaces below the notepad.
- **D.** Take 25 money and put it on your notepad.
- **E.** Draw 2 Final Scoring cards and place them next to your zoo map. You may look at them at any time, but keep them hidden from other players.
- **F.** Draw 8 Zoo cards; keep 4 as hand cards and discard the other 4 to a face-up discard pile on the board. Keep hand cards hidden. (Tip from the rulebook: choose 1–2 Sponsor and 2–3 Animal cards without conditions you cannot fulfill early, ideally matching the Base Conservation Projects on display.)
- **G.** After everyone has chosen their hand cards, reveal the 6 cards of the display.

**Map A bonuses:** its seven support-token bonuses, from top to bottom, are snap one display card, build a size-2 standard enclosure free, gain five money, gain one conservation, gain two reputation, gain twelve money and gain three X-tokens. The first four are received immediately when uncovered and again as break income; the last three are one-time. Take a chosen bonus before or after its project's reward. On Map A the second partner zoo upgrades a card, the third hires a worker and the fourth grants two conservation. The second university upgrades a card and the third grants two conservation. Other maps use their printed bonuses.

4. **Replenish display:** discard the two bottom cards of the display (folders 1 and 2), move the remaining cards down, and refill the display.
5. **Take income** (when multiple players take display cards, **refill the display after each player**; usually simultaneous; if effects require an order, begin with the player who initiated the break — or the affected player closest to them — and proceed clockwise):
   - a. Money according to your zoo's **appeal** (the amount printed next to your counter on the Appeal track; e.g., space 7 pays 11 money).
   - b. **Kiosk income:** for each kiosk, take 1 money per unique building, special enclosure, **occupied** standard enclosure, and pavilion adjacent to it (sharing at least one side of a space). An empty standard enclosure provides no income, but an empty special enclosure does.
   - c. All income marked with the break-income icon on your Sponsor cards and on your **activated** zoo-map bonuses (those uncovered by supporting conservation projects).
   **When more than one player receives a display card during break income, resolve those players clockwise starting with the break initiator (or the first affected player clockwise from them). Refill the display after each such player's income before the next affected player chooses.** This ordering and the between-player refill apply together.

**Reputation track and display:** whenever you increase reputation, advance your counter 1 step. Reaching a space with a bonus grants that bonus immediately, once. Reputation 10+ requires the upgraded Cards action (reminder icon on space 10 / folder 5). If your counter is on space 15 and you gain more reputation, it stays on 15 and you take **1 appeal per remaining reputation step**. "Within reputation range" = the display card on the folder matching your counter plus all lower-numbered folders. After a turn in which display cards were taken: move cards from higher-numbered folders down (keeping their order), then fill empty spaces from the deck. You may not look through the discard pile during the game.

- **Conservation project work (strength 5):** choose either to support a conservation project already in play, or to play a Conservation Project card from your hand and support it immediately.
    - **New-card sources:** use your hand. With Association II, you may instead use a display card within reputation range and pay its folder number as an additional cost; do not replenish the display until turn end.
    - **Enter play:** put the new card on the leftmost space above the Association board; push existing cards one place right.
    - **Overflow:** depending on player count there can be up to 2, 3, or 4 cards above the board (e.g., 3 with three players). If the new card exceeds the limit, discard the rightmost card. Return its player tokens to their owners' supplies, not to their zoo maps; their map bonuses stay activated.
    - **Base Conservation Projects:** the projects below the board never move and are never replenished, even when fully supported.
    - **Two separate support limits:** a reward level is available only if **no player at all** has a token on it. Each level can hold **one token total across all players**. Separately, you normally may support a particular project only once, even if another level is free. Thus an opponent's token blocks that level too; having no token of your own on the level is insufficient.
    - **Support procedure:**
      1. **Fulfill the chosen condition printed on the card**, and choose a reward level that has no player token on it. If you fulfill several conditions, choose one. You may support each project only once, never one already holding your token.
      2. Take one player token of your choice from the left edge of your zoo map and put it on the chosen condition.
      3. Gain the depicted conservation reward and any depicted reputation. Removing the map token activates its uncovered bonus: take it immediately, before or after the project reward at your choice.
      4. **Recurring bonus:** if the uncovered map bonus is marked as recurring income, gain that same bonus again in every break.

- **2 conservation points:** either upgrade one of your Action cards (flip it) or activate an additional association worker (take a lying worker from the lowest space below the notepad onto the notepad). Each player who reaches space 2 gets this choice.
- **5 and 8 conservation points:** take either 5 money or one of the Bonus tiles next to that space. Execute a chosen tile immediately, then remove it from the game. The 5-money option remains even after both Bonus tiles there are gone.
- **10 conservation points:** the first time any player reaches or exceeds 10, **all players** choose and discard one of their Final Scoring cards (face down under the remaining pile). If no one reaches 10 conservation points before the game ends, all players must discard one Final Scoring card before end-game scoring begins.

- **Display timing:** whenever you take cards from the display (snap, or upgraded Cards/Animals/Association/Sponsors plays), do not replenish it until your entire turn is complete; then slide cards down folders in order and refill from the deck. **During the break, at step 4 before income**, discard folder 1 and 2 cards, compact the remaining cards and refill the display.

- **Discarded conservation projects:** tokens on a project card pushed off the display return to the owners' **supply**, not to the bonus spaces on their zoo maps (the bonuses stay activated).
- **2-player game:** one level on each face-up Base Conservation Project and the left column of the donation area are blocked for both players.
- **Association worker supply:** hire workers from the lowest supply space upward; certain zoo maps reward conservation points for hiring your last worker.

- **Flock Animal:** if another herbivore in your zoo requires at least the flock animal's standard-enclosure size, you need not flip an empty enclosure. The same qualifying herbivore can host any number of flock animals and need not itself be a flock animal. Without a qualifying herbivore, house the flock animal normally; a later non-flock herbivore cannot join it in that enclosure. Releasing a flock animal still frees an occupied enclosure under the release/fallback procedure even if the flock animal originally shared. Exact historical residents are not tracked.

- **Score:** discard a Final Scoring card if no one hit 10 conservation points → score end-game cards and Final Scoring cards (max 4 conservation points each) → **VP = Appeal − lowest Appeal value in your Conservation counter's scoring area**. Highest positive VP wins; ties: most conservation projects supported, then shared victory.

judgments.question: How may a Conservation Project enter play, what are support conditions/once limits, where does its token come from, when is the uncovered bonus taken, and what happens to overflowing projects/tokens?

Meet a printed condition and choose a reward level with no token from any player. Removing the token activates its map bonus; take that bonus immediately before or after the project reward as chosen. 5. If a project above the board is pushed off through overflow, return its support tokens to their owners’ supplies; their map bonuses stay activated.
